summary: Admit the bounded Russian Post operation that restores formed-batch orders to the provider backlog.

impacts.evidence: The authenticated route resolves the logistics account inside the request workspace and the operation receipt is tenant-scoped.
Only bounded provider order references, status and observation time cross the adapter boundary; no provider payload or credentials are persisted.
A new additive OpenAPI operation and generated SDK method expose the restore request and normalized result.
The operation uses the existing approval and operation receipt path and does not change an existing event envelope.
The neutral logistics port and generated SDKs add the bounded order-restore capability.
Existing operation receipts and capability settings are reused; no schema change is required.
The route requires approval, capability and idempotency; the adapter uses callback-scoped credentials and fixed HTTPS egress.
The new state-changing provider operation is explicitly write-sensitive and approval-bound.
The existing operation and approval records provide the authoritative execution lineage.
The host rejects partial acknowledgements and prevents a second external call for an ambiguous operation receipt.
Only the documented Russian Post HTTPS endpoint is admitted; no inbound webhook is added.
The shared host transport bounds the request/response and normalizes provider failures.
Removing the new capability or route closes restore without affecting cancellation or batch formation.
Transport, connector, registry and API tests cover success, partial acknowledgement rejection and admission boundaries.
